# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**From:**
Harper Novak
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]

**To:**
[Name of managed-care plan or state Medicaid appeals unit, as printed on my denial letter]
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**Copy to:** Georgia Department of Community Health / Georgia Medicaid [state agency appeals address]

**RE: Appeal of Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-07-31**
- **Member:** Harper Novak
- **Member ID:** W970661607
- **Reference number:** POC-321500D934-38813
- **Denied service:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
- **Plan:** Medicaid (Medicaid), State of Georgia
- **Appeal deadline stated in my notice:** must be received by 2027-01-27

---

## A note on the governing policy

My denial notice states that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not identify that policy by title, and no policy language has been provided to me. **Because of that, I am not quoting any plan criteria in this letter — I have not been given any to quote.** I am instead setting out the documentation in my record and asking the plan to identify the standard it applied. Please read this letter with that in mind: nothing below should be taken as a quotation of the plan's rules, because the plan has not supplied them.

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130) and asking for reconsideration. The reason given was that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the prior authorization packet contains a complete record of my symptoms, the treatments I have already tried, my imaging, my physical exam, and my day-to-day function. I am respectfully asking the plan to re-review that record in full, and — if something specific is genuinely missing — to tell me and my surgeon in writing exactly what it is.

## Request for the criteria the plan applied

This is the heart of my appeal, and it is a request the plan is in the best position to answer: **please provide me, in writing, with the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization request for CPT 27130.** The plan holds those criteria; I do not. I cannot show that my records satisfy a documentation standard I have never been shown, and I cannot know which element the plan considered missing until the plan names it. I am copying the Georgia Medicaid agency on this request. If the criteria are maintained by a review vendor rather than by the plan directly, please identify the vendor and provide the criteria it used.

## The documentation that is in my record

Below is what the prior authorization packet contains. I have not added anything to it, and I am not stating any threshold as the plan's requirement, because the plan has not stated a threshold to me.

**Duration and course of symptoms.** Nine months of progressive pain in the hip, unrelieved by rest.

**Supervised conservative care.** Supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait: 8 weeks, from 2026-04-09 to 2026-06-04, with 20 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

**Medication and injection trials.** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-12 gave 2 weeks of partial relief.

**Imaging.** Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated 2026-06-13: joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.

**Physical examination.** Positive provocative testing on the affected side; range of motion limited by pain.

**Functional status.** I walk with a cane and am limited to about one block. I cannot put on my shoes without help.

**Surgical safety factors.** No active infection. No untreated substance use. BMI 29. Non-smoker.

**Treating surgeon.** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery.

## Why I am asking for reconsideration

The denial rests on the completeness of the documentation, not on a finding that my hip does not need surgery. The record above documents how long I have had symptoms, what non-surgical treatment I completed and when, what medications and injection I tried and how little relief they gave, what my radiograph shows, what my exam shows, how limited my walking and self-care have become, and that I have no infection or other factor that would make surgery unsafe. Each of those is a dated, sourced entry from my chart, and my surgeon has documented that the procedure is needed.

If the plan maintains that a specific item is still missing, I ask that the plan name that item in writing so that my surgeon can supply it. If the plan is relying on a documentation requirement that my record does in fact meet, I ask that the denial be overturned on reconsideration.

## Closing request

Please reconsider and overturn the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27130 and authorize the procedure. Along with your decision, please send me (1) the clinical criteria applied to this request, and (2) a specific written list of any documentation the plan still considers missing.

I understand from my notice that my appeal must be received by 2027-01-27, and I am submitting this letter to the appeal address printed on that notice. I also understand that I may appeal through my state Medicaid agency or my managed-care plan and that I may request a state fair hearing; the contact details are in my denial letter, and I can also reach the plan by phone at the number on the back of my insurance card. I recognize that Medicaid appeal timeframes can be shorter than 180 days in some circumstances, so I am acting well ahead of the date my notice gives.

Thank you for taking a second look at this. Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further from me would help.

Sincerely,

**Harper Novak**
Member ID: W970661607
[Signature]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:** [List what you send — e.g., copy of the 2026-07-31 denial notice; physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-06-04; radiograph report dated 2026-06-13; office notes from Dr. Lindqvist; medication and injection records]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.submission_route: Medicaid is run by your state. Appeal through your state Medicaid agency or your managed-care plan, and you can also ask for a state fair hearing. All of the details are on your denial letter. By phone: the number on the back of your insurance card Deadline: Often just 30 to 90 days — act quickly and check your letter -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Most state Medicaid programs publish the rules for HOW a decision must be made but not the medical criteria for a specific surgery - those usually sit with your managed-care plan or its review vendor. Ask your plan in writing for 'the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization', and copy your state Medicaid agency. Massachusetts, North Carolina and California are the exceptions - they publish real procedure criteria.
